clue.text: From wandering minstrel to a modern conductor.

indicators.note: wandering suggests the letters of the words that follow roam about into a new order

explanation.surface: A travelling medieval singer is set beside a present-day orchestral maestro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges MINSTREL, TO and A (eleven letters) into SIMON RATTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Simon Rattle is a celebrated contemporary British orchestra director, formerly of the Berlin Philharmonic.

clue.text: Holly is one above the law

indicators.note: in a down entry, above places the first piece over the one that follows

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
lex is the Latin word for law

explanation.surface: Someone named Holly thinks the rules do not apply to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'above' sets I on top of LEX in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the botanical genus of the holly tree.

clue.text: Person turning sour and 0 oppressive

parts.note: one means a person, as in 'one never knows'

indicators.note: turning here means souring milk is churned, so its letters change places

explanation.surface: Someone going sour becomes a burden to those around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' is the anagram signal, playing on milk turning sour. The printed '0' is an OCR remnant of a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something onerous is burdensome, a weight pressing down on those who bear it.

clue.text: Form of pear harvest

indicators.note: a form of a word is that word reshaped, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of pear is gathered at harvest time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' rearranges PEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to gather in a crop, the work of the harvest.

clue.text: Army contractor?

parts.note: read not as a military supplier but as something in the arm that contracts: a muscle

explanation.surface: A firm supplying goods to the military.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army' means 'of the arm', not 'military'; the muscle at the back of the upper arm contracts to straighten it.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the upper-arm muscle whose contraction extends the elbow.

clue.text: Half-moon river

explanation.surface: A crescent moon reflected over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A lune is a crescent shape like a half-moon, and the Lune is a river in north-west England flowing through Lancaster.

clue.text: One gets cross when people are standing

definitions.text: One gets cross when people are standing

parts.words: One gets cross when people are standing
parts.note: read 'cross' as the X a voter marks and 'standing' as being candidates in an election

explanation.surface: Someone grows irritable when made to stand around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' and 'standing' like being on one's feet; the voter marks an X beside candidates standing for office.
explanation.definitionFit: A voting slip is marked with an X for one of those standing for election.

clue.text: … disclosures from the last book

explanation.surface: Secrets are leaked from the final volume of a series.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelations are things made known; the Book of Revelation, often called Revelations, closes the Bible.

clue.text: That part of the house to be papered?

definitions.text: That part of the house to be papered?

parts.words: That part of the house to be papered?
parts.note: read 'papered' not as wallpapered but as supplied with newspapers to read

explanation.surface: Deciding which room needs new wallpaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'papered' suggests decorating; the room meant is one stocked with newspapers and periodicals.
explanation.definitionFit: A library or club room set aside for quiet perusal of newspapers and books.

clue.text: No.I dressing-room of the old Royal Court

explanation.surface: The lead actor's dressing room in an old royal theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The top performer gets the star's room backstage; the Star Chamber was a Tudor and Stuart English court abolished in 1641.

clue.text: Reasonable mince-pies, nix even!

indicators.note: to mince is to chop finely, so the letters of the following words are chopped up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Mince pies are a fair price, nothing even about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince', the front of 'mince-pies', chops up PIES, NIX and EVEN (eleven letters) into INEXPENSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasonable price is a modest one, cheap rather than costly.

clue.text: Copy unknown quantity what's the point!

parts.note: to ape is to copy or mimic
X is the algebraic symbol for an unknown

explanation.surface: Someone imitating an unknown figure wonders what the purpose is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's the point' looks like a sigh of futility; it defines the tip or peak.
explanation.definitionFit: An apex is the highest point or tip of something.

clue.text: Quarter to noon-timefor school

parts.note: E, east, is one quarter of the compass
N is a standard abbreviation for noon in timetables

explanation.surface: At a quarter to twelve it is time to go to school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarter to noon' looks like a clock time; it is the compass quarter E, then TO, then N for noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is the famous English boarding institution near Windsor.

clue.text: Unusually bald guy spotted beetle

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of the next words are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An oddly hairless man was seen by a beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges BALD and GUY into LADYBUG.
explanation.definitionFit: The ladybug, or ladybird, is a small round insect with a red, black-spotted shell.

clue.text: Composer leaving key to chance?

parts.note: G is a musical key
luck means chance or fortune

explanation.surface: A composer leaves the choice of key to fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving key to chance' is read as G left to LUCK, the key letter put before fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Christoph Willibald Gluck was an eighteenth-century German opera writer, author of Orfeo ed Euridice.

clue.text: 11 with garbled essay for the Kiwis

definitions.note: a plural phrase for a genus name: the genus covers all the kiwis

indicators.note: garbled means jumbled, so the combined letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 11 across, a peak or tip
an essay is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: Someone joins a muddled piece of writing for New Zealanders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garbled' mixes APEX (from 11) with TRY ('essay' as an attempt). 'the Kiwis' suggests New Zealanders but means the flightless birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Apteryx is the zoological genus containing the flightless birds of New Zealand.

clue.text: Type of quartz found in an opening in the wall of the b city

parts.words: opening in the wall of the b city
parts.note: a gate is an entrance through a city wall; 'b' is an OCR remnant of 'old'

explanation.surface: A gemstone is discovered in a gateway through an ancient city wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded variety of chalcedony, a microcrystalline mineral of silica.

clue.text: Vessel containing its record of big hits

indicators.note: containing means the ship holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: SS, steamship, prefixes a vessel's name
a log is a ship's record

explanation.surface: A ship carries its logbook listing major strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' is the container signal; SS stands for steamship before a vessel's name, and 'big hits' are wild swipes, as in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Slogs are hard, wild blows, as in cricket where a batsman hits out.

clue.text: Chinese set fashion at Gateshead

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or style, as in 'bon ton'
read as Gates' head, the first letter of Gates

explanation.surface: A Chinese group sets a trend in a north-east English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England; split as Gates-head it gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: A tong is a Chinese secret society or association, a closed group.

clue.text: Twisted hose found in Oxford for example

indicators.note: twisted means wrung out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A tangled stocking is turned up in the university city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' rearranges HOSE. 'Oxford' looks like the city; an oxford is a lace-up brogue.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxford is a style of laced leather footwear.

clue.text: Keen copper in tea-break

indicators.note: in puts the metal's symbol inside the broken-up word
break means the word tea is broken apart and its letters reassembled

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: An eager policeman is on his tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges the drink into ATE, and 'in' sets the metal's symbol inside. 'copper' looks like a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute senses are sharp and keen.

clue.text: Unite in medley-race, etc

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Swimmers come together in a medley relay and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medley' mixes RACE and ETC into ACCRETE.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to grow together or join into one mass.

clue.text: See me in red perhaps, dressed like a lord

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone invites you to see them in scarlet robes, like a peer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ME, IN and RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers' ceremonial robes are trimmed with white stoat fur.

clue.text: Needing flying doctor?

parts.note: read not as calling the outback air medical service but as feeling ill from flying

explanation.surface: Someone in the outback requiring the air ambulance service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying doctor' suggests Australia's airborne medical service; the patient needs a doctor because of flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea brought on by travelling in an aircraft.

clue.text: Dutch scholar in epoch which has number work put back

parts.note: an era is an epoch

indicators.note: put back means the arithmetic is turned round and read in reverse

parts.note: sums are arithmetic, work with numbers

explanation.surface: A Dutch academic of his age returns to arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' is the reversal signal; 'number work' is arithmetic, the totals schoolchildren do.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderius Erasmus of Rotterdam was the leading Renaissance humanist thinker.

clue.text: Archbishop's gown wrong way round!

definitions.note: possessive: the signature of the Archbishop of York

indicators.note: wrong way round means the garment's name is read backwards

parts.note: a robe is a gown

explanation.surface: A churchman's vestment has been put on backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong way round' reverses ROBE. Ebor, from Latin Eboracum, is how the Archbishop of York signs his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Archbishop of York signs with the abbreviated Latin name of his see.

clue.text: Got up as a symbol of wars

explanation.surface: Someone stood up as an emblem of conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is the past of rise, to get up; red and white roses were the emblems of the English Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Smoking pipe can bring respiratory infection to English

indicators.note: to joins the abbreviation onto the end of the illness

parts.note: flu, influenza, infects the airways

explanation.surface: A smoker's pipe can give an Englishman a chest infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoking pipe' suggests tobacco; it is a chimney duct carrying smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A flue is a duct for smoke from a fire or furnace.

clue.text: Some undervalued diesel fuel

indicators.note: some means only part of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A portion of diesel is priced too low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run from inside 'undervalued'.
explanation.definitionFit: Derv, from diesel-engined road vehicle, is the British name for diesel for road use.

clue.text: Chapter head for article in study

indicators.note: in puts the article inside the word for a study

parts.note: a den is a private study
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The first heading of a chapter is an article in a study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chapter head' looks like a heading in a book; it is the head of a cathedral chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean presides over the chapter, the governing clergy body of a cathedral.

clue.text: Advance dealer not recommended by Polonius?

explanation.surface: A man trading in loans whom a Shakespearean adviser would disapprove of.
explanation.definitionFit: One who deals in advances of cash; Polonius in Hamlet advises 'Neither a borrower nor a lender be'.

clue.text: Eternally firn-splitting

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Eternally firn-splitting', is garbled: 'firn-splitting' gives no parse for NEVER-ENDING, and 'Eternally' is an adverb against an adjective answer.
